intro.line: Five builds, each flipped over to show the decision that made it work.

items.alt: A man in a VR headset holds two controllers while colleagues watch his view on a laptop screen beside him.
items.label: MetaHRise
items.body: The laptop mirror mattered as much as the headset: people waiting their turn were already learning the space before they put it on.

items.alt: A phone held up towards a colonial-era building shows an animated guide character on its screen.
items.label: CheritAR
items.body: The building does the storytelling. The phone only answers the question a passer-by already has, which is why nobody needs instructions.

items.alt: Visitors stand in a darkened room with woven patterns projected across every wall.
items.label: IKAT Malaysia
items.body: Putting the pattern on the walls instead of behind glass turned textile history into somewhere you stand inside. The scale is the argument.

items.alt: A crowd on a city street at night holds up phones towards a building facade.
items.label: ARFestKL
items.body: An AR trail is a crowd-flow problem before it's a content problem: each point went where people could stop, not where the view was best.

items.alt: A visitor touches a large wall display showing archival photographs.
items.label: Founders' Gallery
items.body: A permanent gallery has to survive its ten-thousandth visitor, so the interaction is one gesture deep and the depth lives in the stories.
